Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: The most valuable and extensive possessions were those in Sicily, around Syracuse and Palermo.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: The revenues from these properties in Sicily and Lower Italy were estimated at three and one-half talents of gold in the eighth century, when Byzantine Emperor Leo the Isaurian confiscated them.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: But the patrimonies in the vicinity of Rome (the successors to the classical latifundia in the Ager Romanus), which had begun to form in the 7th century, were the most numerous.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Most of the remote patrimonies were lost in the eighth century, so the patrimonia around _____ began to be managed with especial care, headed up by deacons directly subordinate to the pope
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: But the patrimonies in the vicinity of Rome (the successors to the classical latifundia in the Ager Romanus), which had begun to form in the 7th century, were the most numerous. Most of the remote patrimonies were lost in the eighth century, so the patrimonia around Rome began to be managed with especial care, headed up by deacons directly subordinate to the pope.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Peter, Pope Gregory (540-604) showed a considerable grasp of detail and administrative capacity.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Peter, Pope Gregory (540-604) showed a considerable grasp of detail and administrative capacity. In anticipation of a threatened corn shortage, Gregory filled the granaries of Rome with the harvests of Egypt and Sicily.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Since the partition of the empire, the Western emperors had preferred to make the better-protected Ravenna their residence.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Here was the centre of _____'s power and of the Ostrogothic rule; here also, after the fall of the Ostrogoths, the viceroy of the Byzantine emperor in Italy, the exarch, resided
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Here was the centre of Odoacer's power and of the Ostrogothic rule; here also, after the fall of the Ostrogoths, the viceroy of the Byzantine emperor in Italy, the exarch, resided.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Cassiodorus, as praefectus praetorio under the _____ supremacy, entrusted the care of temporal affairs to Pope John II
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Here was the centre of Odoacer's power and of the Ostrogothic rule; here also, after the fall of the Ostrogoths, the viceroy of the Byzantine emperor in Italy, the exarch, resided. Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: When Emperor Justinian issued the Pragmatic Sanction of 554, the pope and the Senate were entrusted with the control of weights and measures.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: The popes were now the only court of judicature, a task more often entrusted to bishops as "Defensor populi".

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: In AD 715 the papal chair, which had last been occupied by seven Eastern popes, was filled by a Westerner, Pope Gregory II, who was destined to oppose Leo III the Isaurian in the Iconoclastic conflict.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: In 751 _____ conquered Ravenna, and thereby decided the long delayed fate of the exarchate and the Pentapolis
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: In 751 Aistulf conquered Ravenna, and thereby decided the long delayed fate of the exarchate and the Pentapolis. And when Aistulf, who held Spoleto also under his immediate sway, directed all his might against the Duchy of Rome, it seemed that this too could no longer be held.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

And when Aistulf, who held Spoleto also under his immediate sway, directed all his might against the Duchy of Rome, it seemed that this too could no longer be held.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: The Franks alone were powerful enough to compel the _____ to maintain peace, and they alone stood in close relationship with the pope
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Byzantium could send no troops, and Emperor Constantine V, in answer to the repeated requests for help of the new pope, Stephen II, could only offer him the advice to act in accordance with the ancient policy of Byzantium, to pit some other Germanic tribe against the Lombards. The Franks alone were powerful enough to compel the Lombards to maintain peace, and they alone stood in close relationship with the pope.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Pope Zachary had only recently (751), at Pepin's accession to the _____ throne, spoken the word that removed all doubts in favour of the Carolingian mayor of the palace
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Pope Zachary had only recently (751), at Pepin's accession to the Merovingian throne, spoken the word that removed all doubts in favour of the Carolingian mayor of the palace.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: It was not unreasonable, therefore, to expect an active show of gratitude in return, when Rome was most grievously pressed by _____
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: It was not unreasonable, therefore, to expect an active show of gratitude in return, when Rome was most grievously pressed by Aistulf. Accordingly, Stephen II secretly sent a letter to king Pepin by pilgrims, soliciting his aid against Aistulf and asking for a conference.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Accordingly, _____ II secretly sent a letter to king Pepin by pilgrims, soliciting his aid against Aistulf and asking for a conference
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Accordingly, Stephen II secretly sent a letter to king Pepin by pilgrims, soliciting his aid against Aistulf and asking for a conference. While Pope Stephen was preparing for the journey, a messenger arrived from Constantinople, bringing to the pope the imperial mandate to treat once more with Aistulf for the purpose of persuading him to surrender his conquests.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Pepin in turn sent _____ of Jumièges to confer with the pope, and a little later dispatched Duke Autchar and Bishop Chrodegang of Metz to conduct the pope to the Frankish realm
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Pepin in turn sent Abbot Droctegang of Jumièges to confer with the pope, and a little later dispatched Duke Autchar and Bishop Chrodegang of Metz to conduct the pope to the Frankish realm.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: Never before had a pope crossed the _____
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Never before had a pope crossed the Alps.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Stephen took with him the imperial messenger and several dignitaries of the Roman Church, as well, as members of the aristocracy belonging to the Roman militia, and proceeded first of all to Aistulf.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: The pope then went to St-Denis, near Paris.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: He concluded a firm alliance of friendship with Pepin and made him the first _____ king, probably in January 754
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: He concluded a firm alliance of friendship with Pepin and made him the first Carolingian king, probably in January 754. He bound the Franks under the threat of excommunication, never thereafter to choose their kings from any other family than the Carolingian.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: He bound the _____ under the threat of excommunication, never thereafter to choose their kings from any other family than the Carolingian
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: He bound the Franks under the threat of excommunication, never thereafter to choose their kings from any other family than the Carolingian. In their stead now the King of the Franks was to be the protector of the Romans and their Bishop.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: This became imperative, when several embassies attempted by peaceful means to induce the _____ king to give up his conquests but returned without accomplishing their mission
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: This became imperative, when several embassies attempted by peaceful means to induce the Lombard king to give up his conquests but returned without accomplishing their mission.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Patrimony of Saint Peter.question: At Quiercy on the Oise, the _____ nobles finally gave their consent
Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: At Quiercy on the Oise, the Frankish nobles finally gave their consent.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: Pepin promised in writing to give the Church certain territories, the first documentary record for the States of the Church.

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: The Lombard promised to give up the cities of the exarchate and of the Pentapolis, which had been last conquered, to make no further attacks upon or to evacuate the Duchy of Rome and the northwest Italian districts of Venetia and Istria, and also acknowledged the sovereignty of the Franks. Patrimony of Saint Peter.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Patrimony of Saint Peter.fact: The Byzantine Government naturally did not approve of this result of Frankish intervention.

Paškal Buconjić.fact: In December 1881, however, Custos Zovko wrote to the Order's General about the parishes in Herzegovina. The General asked Zovko about the right of possession of those parishes.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Zovko replied in February _____ that the Franciscans had established and controlled those parishes and, therefore, had patronage over them
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Zovko replied in February 1882 that the Franciscans had set up and controlled those parishes and, therefore, had patronage over them.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Begić informed the General about the agreement in July _____; he received no reply, so he wrote again in March 1885, when Buconjić was supposed to visit Rome and settle the issue
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The new Custos Luka Begić, who was elected in May 1883, became concerned that the position of the Franciscans would be endangered, even if only the diocese controlled the newly-established parishes, and insisted that even those parishes should belong to the Franciscan Custody. Begić informed the General about the agreement in July 1883; he received no reply, so he wrote again in March 1885, when Buconjić was supposed to visit Rome and settle the issue.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The Propaganda received Begić's request in June _____ and informed the State Secretariat about the issue
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Buconjić and Begić arrived in Rome on 12 May 1885. The Propaganda received Begić's request in June 1885 and informed the State Secretariat about the issue.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: In December _____, Vannutelli asked Buconjić whether he agreed with Begić's proposal to write which parishes the Franciscans should retain and which should be at his disposal
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Buconjić and Begić arrived in Rome on 12 May 1885. The Propaganda received Begić's request in June 1885 and informed the State Secretariat about the issue.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Paškal Buconjić.fact: Secretary of State Cardinal Luigi Jacobini asked Nuncio Cardinal Serafino Vannutelli in Vienna to ask Buconjić about the parishes the Franciscans were supposed to retain and those that were at his disposal. Paškal Buconjić.fact: Secretary of State Cardinal Luigi Jacobini asked Nuncio Cardinal Serafino Vannutelli in Vienna to ask Buconjić about the parishes the Franciscans were supposed to retain and those that were at his disposal. In December 1885, Vannutelli asked Buconjić whether he agreed with Begić's proposal to write which parishes the Franciscans should retain and which should be at his disposal.

Paškal Buconjić.fact: Lupori advised Friar Nikola Šimović to explain the Franciscans' position on the matter to the Nuncio in Vienna and to get a confirmation for their proposal.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: At the end of _____ 1889, he visited the Nuncio, who told him he would try to resolve the matter in the interest of the Franciscans
Paškal Buconjić.fact: At the end of October 1889, he visited the Nuncio, who told him he would try to resolve the matter in the interest of the Franciscans.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Paškal Buconjić.fact: After returning to Mostar, Šimović wrote to the Nuncio again, reminding him of Radoš's proposal from 1888.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The Nuncio replied in _____ 1889, promising to support such a proposal
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The Nuncio replied in December 1889, promising to support such a proposal.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: In 1892, the _____ of Herzegovina was elevated to a province
Paškal Buconjić.fact: In 1892, the Franciscan Custody of Herzegovina was elevated to a province.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Custos Rafael Radoš was supposed to join Buconjić in Rome, but died in March _____
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Buconjić was supposed to visit Rome after Easter in 1899, which Begić saw as an opportunity to resolve the issue of parishes. Custos Rafael Radoš was supposed to join Buconjić in Rome, but died in March 1899.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Begić wrote to the General of the Order in April that year to represent the _____ in Herzegovina
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Begić wrote to the General of the Order in April that year to represent the Franciscan Province in Herzegovina.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Pope Leo XIII confirmed the _____ on 17 July 1899; 14 parishes were designated to the diocesan clergy while others were left to the Franciscans
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Pope Leo XIII confirmed the Decisia on 17 July 1899; 14 parishes were designated to the diocesan clergy while others were left to the Franciscans. The beginning of this publication states, "We considered it adequate to present before the eyes of the priests of our dioceses, and especially to the young ones, the copies of the solemn Decisia about the parishes set up or those ought to be established.

Paškal Buconjić.fact: At the time, Trebinje-Mrkan was administered by the Bishop of Dubrovnik. During the talks about the organization of the Church in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Governor of Dalmatia General Gavrilo Rodić and Bishop of Dubrovnik Ivan Zaffron opposed the idea that Trebinje-Mrkan should be exempted from the Bishop of Dubrovnik.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Paškal Buconjić.fact: The churches and schools were renovated and rebuilt, and the number of Catholics in the territory increased.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Still, the _____ population and clergy wanted their bishop
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The churches and schools were renovated and rebuilt, and the number of Catholics in the territory increased. Still, the Catholic population and clergy wanted their bishop.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Zaffron later supported the initiative and proposed Apostolic Vicar of _____ Ćurčija as a new bishop of Trebinje-Mrkan
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Zaffron later supported the initiative and proposed Apostolic Vicar of Egypt Bishop Ljudevit Ćurčija as a new bishop of Trebinje-Mrkan.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: After a year of novitiate, he became a member of the newly established _____ of Herzegovina in 1852
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Paškal Buconjić (2 April 1834 – 8 December 1910) was Herzegovinian Croat Franciscan and a prelate of the Catholic Church who served as the first bishop of Mostar-Duvno from 1881 to 1910, as the apostolic administrator of Trebinje-Mrkan from 1890 to 1910, as the apostolic vicar of Herzegovina from 1880 to 1881, and as custos of the Franciscan Custody of Herzegovina between 1874 and 1879. After a year of novitiate, he became a member of the newly set up Franciscan Custody of Herzegovina in 1852.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: During the _____ of 1875–1877, Buconjić, with Bishop Anđeo Kraljević helped to pacify the Catholic population and supported the occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary
Paškal Buconjić.fact: During the Herzegovina Uprising of 1875–1877, Buconjić, with Bishop Anđeo Kraljević helped to pacify the Catholic population and supported the occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: With the restoration of the regular Church hierarchy in 1881, _____ć was appointed the first Bishop of the newly established Diocese Mostar-Duvno
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Buconjić was important in Croatian politics during the Austro-Hungarian rule in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In 1880, after the Austrian-Hungarian occupation, Buconjić was appointed Apostolic Vicar of Herzegovina and a titular bishop of Magydus and was consecrated in Zagreb the same year.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Jerome was published under the title "Speech on the Occasion of the _____ of the SS Slavic Apostles Cyril and Methodius" in 1863
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Jerome was published under the title "Speech on the Occasion of the Millennial Celebration of the SS Slavic Apostles Cyril and Methodius" in 1863.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: In 1871, he gained the highest _____ academic title of jubilee lecturer
Paškal Buconjić.fact: He visited Pope Pius IX at his residence in Castel Gandolfo and asked him to appoint a Herzegovinian Franciscan as the apostolic vicar. He lectured in Rome until 20 December 1866, when he returned to the Franciscan friary in Široki Brijeg to teach dogma and morals.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Karaula was eventually murdered on 20 _____ 1875
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Karaula was eventually murdered on 20 July 1875.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: In June 1875, _____ started the Herzegovina uprising; Catholics of Gabela, led by Ivan Musić—who was Kraljević's nephew—were the first to rebel
Paškal Buconjić.fact: In June 1875, Christians started the Herzegovina uprising; Catholics of Gabela, led by Ivan Musić—who was Kraljević's nephew—were the first to rebel.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Meanwhile, the uprising spread to the whole of Bosnia and _____ and culminated with the Russo-Turkish War that ended with the Treaty of San Stefano in 1878
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Kraljević and Buconjić helped pacify the Catholics who participated in the uprising because the Catholic leadership viewed the unrest in Herzegovina as a potential struggle for the annexation of these regions to Serbia and Montenegro, respectively. They were successful in their mission; on 19 February 1877, Kraljević informed the Propaganda in Rome that the Catholics of Herzegovina enjoyed "peace and rest".

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The Treaty of _____ was revised at the Congress of Berlin held on 13 July 1878
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The Treaty of San Stefano was revised at the Congress of Berlin held on 13 July 1878.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Paškal Buconjić.fact: Forlani proposed Marijan Zovko for the position of Custos, which the Propaganda approved on 20 June 1879.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The new administration named _____ć guardian of the Humac friary on 18 August 1879
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Buconjić read the Propaganda's decision on 4 August; upon receiving the news, Zovko refused his appointment due to illness. The new administration named Buconjić guardian of the Humac friary on 18 August 1879.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: Pope Leo XIII approved _____ć's nomination and issued two decrees on 30 January 1880 appointing Buconjić the apostolic vicar and a titular bishop of Magydus
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The new administration named Buconjić guardian of the Humac friary on 18 August 1879. Due to his loyalty to Austria-Hungary, the Austrian-Hungarian authorities lobbied for Buconjić to succeed Bishop Kraljević with a recommendation from the apostolic vicar of Bosnia, Bishop Paškal Vuičić.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: From 5 July 1881, _____ XIII with the apostolic bull Ex hac augusta restored the regular Church hierarchy in Bosnia and Herzegovina
Paškal Buconjić.fact: From 5 July 1881, Pope Leo XIII with the apostolic bull Ex hac augusta restored the regular Church hierarchy in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The emperor's appointment was sent to Rome for official confirmation and _____ XIII confirmed the appointment on 18 November 1881, absolving Buconjić of the title of Bishop of Magydus
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The emperor's appointment was sent to Rome for official confirmation and Pope Leo XIII confirmed the appointment on 18 November 1881, absolving Buconjić of the title of Bishop of Magydus.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: He approved the construction of the _____ friary near the redesignated cathedral on April 30, 1886
Paškal Buconjić.fact: Buconjić agreed to make the diocesan cathedral a Franciscan friary church while the new cathedral church was to be built with help from the imperial government. He approved the construction of the Franciscan friary near the redesignated cathedral on April 30, 1886.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The publishing of _____ stopped due to hardship in 1896
Paškal Buconjić.fact: During Buconjić's reign, Glas Hercegovca (the Voice of a Herzegovinian), a political magazine, was set up and was supported by Buconjić and the Herzegovinian Franciscans. The publishing of Glas Hercegovca stopped due to hardship in 1896.

Paškal Buconjić.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Paškal Buconjić.question: The founding session of the _____ for the Needs of Students and University Students from Bosnia and Herzegovina was held on 14 September 1902, and Buconjić was named its sponsor
Paškal Buconjić.fact: The founding session of the Croatian Support Society for the Needs of Students and University Students from Bosnia and Herzegovina was held on 14 September 1902, and Buconjić was named its sponsor. The Croatian Support Society would grow to become HKD Napredak.

Paškal Buconjić.fact: He also set up several parishes: Vinica on 7 May 1885, Posuški Gradac on 28 April 1887; Tihaljina on 19 May 1889, Medjugorje on 1 May 1892, and Nevesinje in 1899.
